recreation_prompts.t2i_start_frame: A wide, locked-off establishing frame, shot at eye level on a city sidewalk at night, of a long single-file queue of roughly a dozen people waiting outside the glass entrance of an upscale restaurant. The crowd is generic, diverse Korean urban adults of mixed ages in autumn outerwear — beige trench coats, padded jackets, knit sweaters, crossbody and tote bags — standing in profile and three-quarter views, shoulders slightly hunched against the evening chill, a few tilting their heads down toward glowing smartphones. They stand patiently, barely moving, strung out along a low nylon queue-barrier rope that runs across the foreground. The restaurant facade behind them is a modern wall of dark brushed metal and tall vertical-blind windows that glow warm amber from the interior. At the centre of the frame a recessed entrance porch frames the doorway, crowned by a small warm cursive neon script sign. The lighting design is a deliberate cool-warm split: the open sidewalk reads cold ambient night blue (#1A1E2A, #5A6472), while a pool of warm tungsten light (#C8741E, #E8A24A) spills out of the doorway and the neon sign, rim-lighting the silhouettes of the waiting people and casting long deep shadows toward the camera. Key light is effectively back-center from the doorway, soft but with a roughly 5:1 key-to-fill ratio producing hard chiaroscuro and crushed blacks (#0E1018). Lens is a moderate wide angle with deep depth of field so the entire queue stays legible; the composition is near-symmetrical, centred on the bright doorway as the vanishing point with the rope leading the eye in. Surfaces: matte wool and nylon coats, reflective glass-and-metal storefront, taut nylon rope. Atmosphere carries a faint cold night haze and a layer of fine cinematic film grain; the mood is one of dull, drawn-out waiting after dark — the universal boredom of standing in line. The very first instant of the frame emerges out of a soft fade up from black, so edges are slightly veiled and the doorway glow is the first thing to resolve. The palette is desaturated blue overall with one saturated warm light pool, a complementary cool-warm relationship anchored by the amber accent (~12% of frame). No on-screen text or graphic overlays are present in this shot. Composition follows Korean ad norms — subjects placed on the rule-of-thirds grid with considered breathing room. The image should read as a single film frame from a high-production Korean lifestyle commercial — restrained, atmospheric, never glossy or HDR.
